text: I'm 1AC on a CSCW submission and the four reviews are all over the place, scores from 2 to 4.5, and I have to write the meta-review by friday. I keep flipping between tabs and losing track of who said what. Reviews are pasted below (R1 is my 2AC, R2-R4 external). Can you build me a page that shows the four reviews together with each reviewer's score and self-rated expertise, the score spread as a small chart, pulls the strengths, weaknesses and questions out of each review and tags them, shows where the reviewers agree and where they don't, and has a box where I write the meta-review and can pull one of those points in with a click instead of retyping it. Recommendation is accept / minor / major / reject.
side by side is unreadable on my laptop with 4 columns. can it toggle between side by side and stacked

the agree/disagree bit just lists every point again. group them by topic and show per topic what each reviewer said. R2 thinks the deployment was effectively 5 months and R3 says a year-long deployment is the strength of the paper, that's exactly the thing I need to surface in the meta. Disagreements at the top please

clicking a point dumps it at the end of my draft. if the draft has headings (strengths / weaknesses / questions etc) put it under the right one. also grey out points that are already in the draft so I don't add them twice. and a button to add the disagreement itself as a line, like 'deployment: R1, R3 strength; R2, R4 weakness'

your extraction missed R3's comment about whether tenants who never joined knew their payments were visible. let me select text in a review and tag it myself as strength/weakness/question with a topic. keep my tags if I reload
can the chart also show a mean weighted by expertise? R2 is the only one who rated themselves expert and the plain mean kind of hides that. show both
